picks.title: Dewey Data (Yale subscription)
picks.why: Check Yale-accessible mobility products for comparable downtown visit estimates from 2019 through 2023.
picks.limitations: Product availability, historical coverage, panel composition, and comparability must be verified; visits are not necessarily pedestrian counts.

resolution.label: good
resolution.reason: Reported by address or point, finer than your tract unit

picks.yale_note: Register at app.deweydata.io with a Yale email; approval can take up to 48 hours. Check the Library list of datasets available at Yale.

picks.title: New Haven Census Tracts 2020
picks.provider: Bureau of the Census (US Census Bureau)
picks.why: Provides consistent geographic reference units for a provisional downtown definition.
picks.limitations: Tracts do not exactly represent downtown and contain no foot-traffic counts.

picks.title: LEHD Origin-Destination Employment Statistics (LODES)
picks.why: Provides workplace employment context for interpreting downtown patterns.
picks.limitations: Annual employment is not a direct measure of office attendance or foot traffic.

resolution.label: good
resolution.reason: Reported by block, finer than your tract unit

methods.name: Season-matched recovery index
methods.why: Compare each 2020–2023 month with the same month in 2019, with consistent coverage and normalization.

methods.name: Boundary and measurement validation
methods.why: Use a consistent downtown polygon and check changes in sensors, mobile panel, and visit definitions.

next_steps: Request 2019–2023 comparable pedestrian counts from the Town Green District.
Verify Yale Dewey access, product coverage, and mobile-panel methodology.
Agree on a downtown boundary before calculating monthly recovery.
